parameters.content:
# Claim Checks | Follow Up Story

Answers update in the Claim Checks bot: for ONE archived story it looks for official and reliable news published after the story's date (or after its last update), says what changed, saves the update in the archive and replies in the chat.

**Called by:** "Story Chat" when the bot opens a story conversation for update (without waiting, so the bot answers "looking" at once). Locked to "Story Chat". Errors go to the central error handler (main chat).
**Sections:** Entry → Search And Read → Judge, Save And Reply.
**Services called:** Postgres (claim_checks.stories, story_updates) · Serper (Google results after the date) · Venice (GLM-5.3 Flash: web search; Kimi K2.6: update writer) · Bright Data (page reads) · Telegram (the Claim Checks bot) · Postgres (claim_checks.conversation_exchanges, conversation_messages) · "Ask Venice" (every model step; backup model GPT-6 Luna).

## Entry

Triggered by: "Story Chat" (When Called By Bot) with story_number, question, chat_id and conversation_id.

What it does, step by step:
1. Store Settings adds the source lists and caps.
2. Read Story From Archive (Postgres) gets the story, every link it already has, and the date to search from.

## Search And Read

Triggered by: runs inline after Entry.

What it does, step by step:
1. Search Google Since Story (Serper, after: the date) and Search Web Since Story (Venice web search) look for news on the story.
2. Build Candidates keeps up to 8 new pages (no platforms, no link the story already has).
3. Read Pages (Bright Data) reads them as HTML; Build Writer Input keeps the part about the story and finds each page's publication date (page metadata, else the address, else Google's date).

## Judge, Save And Reply

Triggered by: runs inline after Search And Read.

What it does, step by step:
1. Write Update (via Ask Venice, Kimi K2.6): what is new, the answer to the question, the key points now, a tier for each page.
2. Build Update Reply counts it as new only with a relevant official or reliable page; every source is shown and saved with its date.
3. Save Update To Archive (Postgres story_updates) → Send Update To Chat (Telegram) → Add Update To Conversation (Postgres): the update becomes part of the story conversation, so the user can ask about it and save it.

parameters.query:
SELECT s.story_number, s.found_on::text AS found_on, s.title, s.label, s.claim, s.explainer, s.search_terms,
  concat_ws(E'\n', s.official_links, s.supporting_links, s.contradicting_links,
    (SELECT string_agg(u.links, E'\n') FROM claim_checks.story_updates u WHERE u.story_number = s.story_number)) AS known_links,
  coalesce((SELECT max(u.asked_on AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Rome')::date::text FROM claim_checks.story_updates u WHERE u.story_number = s.story_number), s.found_on::text) AS since
FROM claim_checks.stories s WHERE s.story_number = $1::int;

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'z-ai-glm-5-3-flash', temperature: 0, max_tokens: 700, messages: [{ role: 'system', content: 'Answer only from the web search results of this request. List official, primary and reliable sources published after the given date about this story: one line per source, the URL first, then what the page adds in at most 20 words. If nothing about it was published after that date, answer exactly: NOT FOUND.' }, { role: 'user', content: 'Story: ' + $('Read Story From Archive').first().json.claim + '\nPublished after: ' + $('Read Story From Archive').first().json.since + ($('Store Settings').first().json.question ? '\nQuestion: ' + $('Store Settings').first().json.question : '') }], venice_parameters: { enable_web_search: 'on', enable_web_citations: true } }) }}

parameters.query: INSERT INTO claim_checks.story_updates (story_number, question, result, found_new, links) VALUES ($1::int, $2, $3, $4::boolean, $5) RETURNING update_id;

value.body:
={{ { model: 'kimi-k2-6', temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 2500, venice_parameters: { disable_thinking: true }, response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: 'story_update', strict: true, schema: {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["found_new", "what_changed", "answer", "status_points", "sources"], "properties": {"found_new": {"type": "boolean"}, "what_changed": {"type": "string"}, "answer": {"type": "string"}, "status_points": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["point", "status", "source"], "properties": {"point": {"type": "string"}, "status": {"type": "string", "enum": ["confirmed", "stated_only", "not_disclosed", "contradicted"]}, "source": {"type": "string"} } } }, "sources": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["n", "tier", "relevant"], "properties": {"n": {"type": "integer"}, "tier": {"type": "string", "enum": ["official", "reliable", "other"]}, "relevant": {"type": "boolean"} } } } } } } }, messages: [{ role: 'system', content: "<role>You follow up ONE news story for a reader who asked what happened since it was first checked. You read pages found after the story's date and say, only from those pages, what is new.</role>

<input>
<story> the story; <label> how it was labelled then; <published_after> the date of the last check; <question> what the reader wants to know; <known_points> what was known then; <pages> pages found now, numbered.
</input>

<rules>
1. Use only the pages. Never your own knowledge of the story. A page counts only if it is about this same story and gives information that is new compared with <known_points> or that answers <question>.
2. For every page give its tier (official: the company, person or body the story is about, a government body, the paper or filing itself; reliable: an established news or trade outlet; other: blogs, forums, copies) and relevant (true only under rule 1).
3. found_new: true only if at least one relevant page is official or reliable. Otherwise false, and what_changed is "".
4. what_changed: 2-4 plain sentences on what is new, naming the source. answer: one or two sentences that answer <question> from the pages, or say plainly that no page answers it yet.
5. status_points: the key points now, each confirmed, stated_only, not_disclosed or contradicted, with the url that shows it ("" if none). Keep a point not_disclosed when no page settles it; never fill it in.
6. Plain English, no hype, no markdown.
</rules>

<example>
<input>
<story>Example Bio says it treated a patient with AI-designed bacteriophages.</story>
<label>Single source</label>
<published_after>2026-10-20</published_after>
<question>Did the patient recover?</question>
<known_points>
- stated_only: The phages were given to a patient
- not_disclosed: Whether the infection cleared
</known_points>
<pages>
<page n="1" url="https://www.nature.com/articles/x">Example Bio's preprint, now peer reviewed, reports that the patient's infection cleared after 14 days of phage treatment...</page>
<page n="2" url="https://someblog.net/post">Is AI phage therapy the future? We think so...</page>
</pages>
</input>
<output>{"found_new":true,"what_changed":"Nature published Example Bio's peer-reviewed results: the patient's infection cleared after 14 days of treatment with the AI-designed phages.","answer":"Yes: according to the peer-reviewed paper in Nature, the infection cleared after 14 days.","status_points":[{"point":"The phages were given to a patient","status":"confirmed","source":"https://www.nature.com/articles/x"},{"point":"The infection cleared","status":"confirmed","source":"https://www.nature.com/articles/x"}],"sources":[{"n":1,"tier":"reliable","relevant":true},{"n":2,"tier":"other","relevant":false}]}</output>
</example>" }, { role: 'user', content: $json.writer_input }] } }}

parameters.query:
-- The update becomes one exchange of the story conversation that asked for it, and its Telegram message is linked to it.
WITH nxt AS (
  SELECT NULLIF($1, '')::int AS conversation_id, coalesce((SELECT max(exchange_no) FROM claim_checks.conversation_exchanges WHERE conversation_id = NULLIF($1, '')::int), 0) + 1 AS exchange_no
  WHERE NULLIF($1, '') IS NOT NULL),
ex AS (
  INSERT INTO claim_checks.conversation_exchanges (conversation_id, exchange_no, question, answer)
  SELECT conversation_id, exchange_no, $2, $3 FROM nxt RETURNING conversation_id, exchange_no),
ln AS (
  INSERT INTO claim_checks.conversation_messages (chat_id, telegram_message_id, conversation_id, exchange_no)
  SELECT $4, NULLIF($5, '')::bigint, conversation_id, exchange_no FROM ex WHERE NULLIF($5, '') IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (chat_id, telegram_message_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING 1)
UPDATE claim_checks.story_conversations SET last_message_at = now()
WHERE conversation_id IN (SELECT conversation_id FROM ex) RETURNING conversation_id;
